A.biggest_strength: True live simulation freedom (continuous learning rate, adjustable initial weight w₀, up to 40 steps, and run/pause animation) paired with simultaneous side-by-side small multiples comparison cards.
A.biggest_weakness: The update step is represented merely as diagonal chords between points on the loss curve rather than showing the horizontal parameter update vector -η·L'(w) along the weight axis, along with formula and table clipping on mobile.

B.biggest_strength: Masterful visual-symbolic decomposition that color-codes every term of the update equation to its geometric primitive (slope as tangent line, step as directed parameter vector, loss as height, and gap to optimum as span).
B.biggest_weakness: Rigid, precomputed sandbox locked to a single starting weight (w₀ = 1), a hard cap of 6 steps, and an intrusive auto-advancing tour that disrupts self-paced study.

structured_output.reasons: Both pages are exceptionally well-crafted, mathematically rigorous, and completely free of factual errors. Page B wins because its visual explanation actually reveals the physical mechanism of gradient descent: rather than just drawing chords across a parabola, it explicitly visualizes the tangent slope, the directional parameter update vector on the w-axis, the landing ghost, and the remaining gap, while binding each term to matching colors across the math, graphics, and numbers. Page B also adds crucial pedagogical depth with its 'What the figure leaves out' guide connecting the 1D toy problem to real-world deep learning practices.
